evidence: Campaign platform commits to policies stopping large corporations from buying up homes en masse (2026 campaign, CalMatters voter guide).
Backs expanding the state's homebuyer down payment assistance program; no stance on broker fees (2026 campaign, CalMatters voter guide).
Backs extending the Prop 30/55 higher income tax rates on high earners for schools (Jan 2026); opposes the separate billionaire wealth tax (Jun 2026).
Supports extending and enforcing the 2019 Tenant Protection Act's rent caps; a related renter policy, not deposit or junk-fee limits (May 2026).
Says families shouldn't face bankruptcy or losing their home over a child's hospital bills; no debt-relief plan (2026 CalMatters candidate Q&A).
Campaign blueprint explicitly opposes introducing voucher programs and notes he opposed Amendment 80, the school-choice measure (May 2026).
Blueprint pledges to ban algorithmic rent collusion by corporate landlords and target mandatory junk fees on renters (May 2026).
Blueprint says he would explore state and philanthropic options to subsidize coverage for families in need; no backfill commitment (May 2026).
Blueprint pledges to fully investigate government fraud, partner with the State Auditor's fraud hotline, and use the False Claims Act; no inspector general (May 2026).
Signed HB 5414, the Reproductive Freedom Defense Act, shielding abortion patients and providers and widening who may provide abortions (May 2022).
Signed an expanded state property tax credit worth about $125 million to middle-class filers and a statewide car-tax cap, per his campaign record (2026).
Signed a cap on insulin at $25 a month and diabetic supplies at $100, per his campaign record; no prior-authorization action found (2020 law, cited 2026).
His 2018 platform proposed a Medicaid buy-in option on the Access Health CT exchange; in 2026 he backs expanding coverage via a narrower CT Option.
2018 platform proposed monthly out-of-pocket drug cost caps and price/rebate disclosure; related to but not a drug-price board; 2026 agenda pledges lower drug costs.
Created Covered Connecticut, no-cost coverage for about 40,000 low-income adults, a related program run through the exchange rather than Medicaid (campaign record, 2026).
Signed HB 94, HB 150 and HB 368, barring state help with federal immigration enforcement in schools, health facilities, courts, churches and hospitals (Sep 2026).
Campaign platform pledged to enshrine reproductive care in Delaware's constitution, and he ran on an abortion-rights amendment (2024 campaign).
Campaigned on universal pre-K for Delaware, per Delaware Public Media reporting cited by Ballotpedia (Nov 2024).
